digest.en: Washington blocked China’s remote access to Nvidia AI chips, triggering immediate diplomatic friction. Seoul’s education minister resigned after an AI cheating scandal swept university exams. These moves highlight how digital governance is now a primary flashpoint for state power.
digest.hi: जेलेंस्की के घर पर पुतिन के ट्रिपल टैप हमले ने यूक्रेन की राजधानी को हिला दिया। इसी घंटे किम जोंग उन ने ट्रंप के फोन को अनसुना करने का फैसला किया। दोनों ही घटनाएं वैश्विक शक्ति संतुलन पर प्रश्नचिह्न खड़ी कर रही हैं।

articles.title: Afghan Women Turn To Social Media To Earn Living As Doors Close Offline
articles.summary: Afghan women are building personal brands on Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube to earn income. They share videos of cooking, shopping, and family gatherings. This digital shift offers a livelihood as offline opportunities have closed under Taliban restrictions. Afghan women who have had their lives sharply restricted by Taliban rule have responded by building personal brands on Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube showing them cooking at home, shopping in bazaars, or meeting friends and family.

articles.title: South Korea Education Minister resigns amid AI cheating scandal
articles.summary: South Korea's Education Minister resigned following an AI cheating scandal. The top scorer in a national tax accountant exam admitted using a miniature camera and smartphone. This confession triggered widespread fears about AI-assisted exam integrity across the country. The country has been gripped by fears of AI-assisted exam cheating since last Sunday (November 15, 2026), when the top scorer in a national tax accountant exam confessed to using a miniature camera and smartphone to achieve a near-perfect score.

articles.title: Immigration officers make arrest at Seattle airport in ‘distressing’ scene, delaying flight
articles.summary: Immigration officers arrested a passenger at Seattle airport, causing a flight delay. The Port of Seattle described the scene as distressing for the family and other passengers. Local authorities are now engaging federal officials to understand what occurred during the incident. The Port of Seattle said in a statement that the arrest was distressing not only for the affected family but for other passengers, and that local authorities would "engage federal officials to understand more about what occurred".

articles.title: U.S. blocks China’s remote access to AI chips after Nvidia scandal; China slams move
articles.summary: The United States blocked China's remote access to AI chips after a Nvidia scandal. The move followed scrutiny of Nvidia's chip sales to Southeast Asian data centers. China condemned the action, citing concerns over founder Jensen Huang's ties to Singapore-based Megaspeed. Nvidia’s provision of chips to companies running data centres in Southeast Asia has come under the spotlight amid questions surrounding founder Jensen Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang, the CEO of one such Singapore-based company, Megaspeed.

articles.title: Pakistan Minister invokes Humayun, Sher Shah at SCO Civilisational Forum
articles.summary: Pakistan's Minister Musadik Malik invoked historical figures Humayun and Sher Shah Suri at the SCO Civilisational Forum. He highlighted the shared heritage of the Purana Qila fort in Delhi. The speech emphasized Timurid and Afghan contributions to the region's architectural history. ‘This [Purana] Qila, where we are sitting, is in itself a story; a fort, whose foundation was laid by Humayun, who had a descent from the Timurid [dynasty] linkage.

articles.title: South Korea education minister resigns after AI cheating scandal engulfs university exams
articles.summary: South Korea's education minister Choi Kyo-jin resigned on Sunday following an AI cheating scandal. He admitted failing to prepare adequately for university entrance exams. The tests banned phones and checked for hidden cameras. The resignation follows widespread fears over AI-assisted fraud in the country's key academic assessments. Choi Kyo-jin said he ‘failed to prepare adequately’ for entrance exams, which this year had phones banned and checks for cameras hidden in clothingSouth Korea’s education minister resigned on Sunday after an AI-assisted cheating scandal that erupted in the lead-up to the country’s key university entrance exams. The country has been gripped by fears of AI-assisted exam cheating since last Sunday, wh.

articles.title: China’s open-weight AI models are coming for America’s market
articles.summary: The Trump administration is considering requiring US companies to disclose their use of Chinese AI models. This move follows growing adoption of tools from DeepSeek, Alibaba, and Moonshot AI. American firms are shifting to these lower-cost alternatives. The deliberation aims to address the rising market share of Chinese open-weight models in the United States. The Trump administration is weighing whether to require American companies to disclose their use of Chinese artificial intelligence, Reuters reported on November 18.

articles.title: Iran To Ration Electricity Amid Warnings Power Grid Battered by US, Israeli Strikes
articles.summary: Iran will begin rationing electricity on November 22. This follows recent bread shortages and purchase management procedures. The move occurs as uncertainty grows over President Trump’s next diplomatic or military step. The government aims to manage domestic resource scarcity. Iran To Ration Electricity As World Awaits Trump's Next Move. Iran To Ration Electricity Amid Warnings Power Grid Battered by US, Israeli Strikes.

articles.title: ‘We escaped with only our lives’: Fighting to give birth in war-torn Yemen
articles.summary: Midwife Anisa Fadhl fled Taiz, Yemen, as fighting escalated two months ago. She left without packing a bag. Her home and clinic were later looted and destroyed. She escaped with only her life. The conflict displaced many medical workers. When fighting suddenly escalated around Taiz, in southwestern Yemen two months ago, midwife Anisa Fadhl had no time to pack a bag before she fled, leaving behind her home and her clinic.

articles.title: Haitians excited but uneasy as El Salvador troops fight gangs
articles.summary: El Salvador deployed troops to Port-au-Prince to combat gangs, drawing mixed reactions from Haitians. Many welcomed the intervention after years of gang control, but others fear the offensive will worsen the volatile security situation in the capital. Foreign combatants in Port-au-Prince welcomed by many after years of gang control but some fear offensive could exacerbate volatile situationA bullet-peppered mural of the Haitian striker Emmanuel Sanon covers the facade of Port-au-Prince’s main football ground.

articles.title: China commits to low-carbon electrification and help for others to improve
articles.summary: China pledged to accelerate low-carbon electrification and assist other nations in doing the same. Wang Yi made the commitment at the Cop31 summit. The goal aligns with broader calls for countries to derive 35% of their energy from electricity by 2035. Exclusive: Countries at Cop31 are being urged to commit to deriving 35% of their energy from electricity by 2035Cop31 live – latest updatesChina is pushing for rapid electrification of its economy using low-carbon energy and will help other countries do the same, a senior member of the Chinese delegation at the Cop31 UN climate summit has said. Wang Yi, a professor of energy and environment policy.

articles.title: Why Takaichi should stick to her guns on Taiwan
articles.summary: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi stated Chinese force against Taiwan could trigger Self-Defense Forces deployment. The remark drew significant criticism from Beijing. China responded with economic and diplomatic pressure against Tokyo. On November 7, 2025, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi was pressed repeatedly in parliament about a possible Chinese invasion or naval blockade of Taiwan. She eventually said that Chinese use of force could trigger the deployment of Japan’s Self-Defense Forces.

articles.title: Trump threatens ‘tremendous penalties’ for US tech firms that build datacenters abroad
articles.summary: Donald Trump threatened to impose severe penalties on American tech firms constructing datacenters outside the United States. He made the statement during a White House press conference on Friday. The president provided no specific details regarding the nature or scale of these penalties. He also admitted he had not yet briefed his own officials on the plan. President gives wide-ranging White House press conference and says he has ‘fantastic relationships’ with Putin and XiDonald Trump threatened on Friday to impose “tremendous penalties” on American tech companies that build datacenters outside the US, though he gave no details and told reporters he had not yet informed his own officials about the plan. In a discursive press conference from the White.

articles.title: Pontoon Bridges, Hydrofoils, Tunnels: Barraged By Russia, Kyiv Rushes For Alternative River
articles.summary: Russia is targeting bridges spanning the Dnieper River in Kyiv. Ukrainian officials are developing alternatives to keep the city connected. Plans include pontoon bridges, hydrofoils, and tunnels. The goal is to prevent the capital from being cut in half. Russia is deliberately targeting the vital bridges that span the Dnieper River -- and link the two sides of Kyiv. Ukrainian officials are scrambling to come up with alternatives in case the city is completely cut in half.

articles.title: With Oil Revenue Running Out, Iran Teases Breaking US Blockade
articles.summary: Iranian hardliners are pushing for a tanker convoy to break the US naval blockade as oil revenue hits zero by mid-December. They threaten to strike Persian Gulf oil sites if the US fires on the vessels. This escalation risks a direct military confrontation in the region. With Iran’s oil revenue set to hit zero by mid-December, IRGC-linked media and hard-liners are pushing for a tanker convoy to break through the US naval blockade, threatening Persian Gulf oil sites if fired on.

articles.title: General Assembly President tells Rohingya refugees after genocide ruling
articles.summary: The President of the United Nations General Assembly visited Cox’s Bazar in Bangladesh one day after the International Court of Justice ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya. The visit aimed to pressure the international community to translate the landmark legal finding into concrete protective measures. The court’s decision marks a significant shift in the diplomatic handling of the crisis. The President urged member states to move beyond rhetoric and implement the court’s directives.

articles.title: Record settler attacks mar olive harvest as UN urges Israel to protect farmers
articles.summary: Israeli settlers carried out over 400 attacks during this year’s West Bank olive harvest. This is the highest number recorded in any previous season. UN agencies and humanitarian groups urged Israel to protect farmers from the violence. The attacks caused casualties and significant property damage. Israeli settlers have carried out more than 400 attacks causing casualties or property damage during this year’s olive harvest in the occupied West Bank – more than in any previous season, UN agencies and humanitarian NGOs said on Friday.

articles.title: Shattered playgrounds and freezing classrooms: Inside Ukraine’s deadliest year for children
articles.summary: UNICEF highlighted record child casualty levels in Ukraine as the country faces another brutal winter. A twice-bombed Kyiv kindergarten stands in ruins during a day-long power cut. Freezing classrooms and shattered playgrounds illustrate the dangers children face. The conflict continues to inflict severe harm on the youngest population. Amid the ruins of a twice-bombed Kyiv kindergarten as a day-long power cut continued, the UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) on Friday highlighted the dangers to youngsters enduring another brutal winter in Ukraine, as child casualty numbers rise to record levels.

articles.title: Countries demand stronger climate deal amid deadlock in Antalya
articles.summary: A coalition of countries challenged the proposed COP31 agreement, demanding explicit fossil fuel action. They also called for stronger climate finance commitments. Tensions rose as the Antalya summit neared its close. Negotiators struggled to find a deal acceptable to nearly 200 governments. A group of countries from Europe, Africa, Latin America and the Pacific has challenged the proposed COP31 agreement, demanding explicit action on fossil fuels and stronger climate finance.

articles.title: Bridgetown AI summit to tackle safety as risks outpace capacity to respond
articles.summary: UN Secretary-General António Guterres co-hosted an AI safety summit in Bridgetown, Barbados. The gathering aimed to close the gap between accelerating technological risks and the limited capacity of many nations to manage the pace of development. UN Secretary-General António Guterres is heading to Barbados to co-host a special summit on artificial intelligence (AI) safety on Monday, aimed at closing the gap between accelerating risks and many countries’ capacity to deal with the pace of development.

articles.title: The secretive ICE force-feeding tactics that ended a Cuban father’s hunger strike
articles.summary: Cuban asylum seeker Luis Alejandro Cora Pérez ended a hunger strike in Texas. He described being force-fed through a tube after five days of resistance. The physical pain forced him to stop the protest. Exclusive: Luis Alejandro Cora Pérez says in messages to Guardian from inside Texas facility pain of force-feeding caused him to break strikeThe text message that came from inside the Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) detention center was stark: “I have spent five days eating regular food.

articles.title: China’s research ships turning ocean science into undersea warfare
articles.summary: China is expanding dual-use oceanographic ship deployments across the Indo-Pacific to map seafloors and track submarines. These vessels operate under scientific cover while threatening undersea cables. The strategy extends Beijing's military reach beyond traditional naval assets. Under the cover of scientific research and deep-sea exploration, China is deploying dual-use survey vessels across the Indo-Pacific to map seafloors, track submarines, and threaten undersea cables, bolstering its military reach.

articles.title: Ambition goes missing as fossil fuel language drops from draft deal
articles.summary: The latest draft climate agreement for COP31 removed explicit language on phasing out fossil fuels. This deletion occurred as ministers and the Presidency attempted to bridge sharp differences before the summit's scheduled close. Civil society groups expressed serious concern over the missing commitment. The change signals a significant retreat in the text's ambition regarding energy transition. A cat named Ambition went missing again at COP31 on Thursday.

articles.title: Battle to control GPS and radio signals raises civilian safety concerns
articles.summary: GPS and radio signals are increasingly blocked or faked, endangering aid convoys, passenger jets, and cargo ships. Civilian safety is declining as these critical navigation systems become unreliable. The disruption affects both conflict zones and open ocean routes. From aid convoys in conflict zones to passenger jets and cargo ships far out at sea, safe journeys depend on GPS, satellite navigation and old-fashioned radio transmissions.

articles.title: A Blown Bridge, A Big Meeting, And A 'Ludicrous Fantasy'
articles.summary: Moscow issued unrealistic European security demands despite losing the Kerch Bridge. The bridge partially collapsed during recent strikes. A meeting of three presidents drew attention. Analysts question the substance of the negotiations. Moscow makes what an analyst called "completely unrealistic" demands about European security despite setbacks in its war on Ukraine -- including the partial destruction of the only bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea.

articles.title: ट्रंप मिलने को तरस रहे, उत्तर कोरिया ने फोन भी नहीं उठाया, अमेरिका को किम जोंग उन ने दिखाया ठेंगा

articles.title: पाकिस्तान-अफगानिस्तान बॉर्डर पर भूकंप से कांपी धरती, शिमला में भी लगे झटके, हिली जमीन
articles.summary: रविवार सुबह पाकिस्तान में 4.0 तीव्रता का भूकंप आया। इसका केंद्र जमीन से 13 किलोमीटर नीचे था। हिमाचल प्रदेश के शिमला में 2.8 तीव्रता के झटके दर्ज किए गए। वहीं, हिमाचल प्रदेश के शिमला जिले में सुबह 6:29 बजे 2.8 तीव्रता के झटके दर्ज किए गए. इससे पहले चंबा में भी भूकंप आया था. शनिवार को पेरू में 6.7 तीव्रता और गुरुवार को जापान के कुमामोटो प्रांत में 5.7 तीव्रता का भूकंप आया था.

articles.title: सिएटल एयरपोर्ट पर ICE की कार्रवाई से हंगामा, फ्लाइट में सवार हो रहे दो लोगों को जेट ब्रिज पर पकड़ा
articles.summary: सिएटल-टैकोमा हवाई अड्डे पर ICE अधिकारियों ने जेट ब्रिज पर दो यात्रियों को पकड़ा। यह कार्रवाई लॉस एंजिलिस जा रही उड़ान के दौरान हुई। घटना से एयरलाइन और राज्य सरकार नाराज हो गई हैं। ICE Agents Seattle Airport: अमेरिका के सिएटल-टैकोमा हवाई अड्डे पर शनिवार सुबह यात्री लॉस एंजिलिस की उड़ान में सवार हो रहे थे, तभी जेट ब्रिज पर नकाबपोश इमिग्रेशन अधिकारियों ने दो लोगों को पकड़ लिया।

articles.title: इंडोनेशिया की कैंडी फैक्टरी में भीषण आग: तीन की मौत; 36 कर्मचारी लापता, अपनों की तलाश में भटक रहे
articles.summary: इंडोनेशिया की एक कैंडी फैक्ट्री में भीषण आग लग गई। इस हादसे में तीन लोगों की मौत हो गई है। 36 कर्मचारी अभी भी लापता हैं। परिजन उनकी तलाश में खोजबीन कर रहे हैं। इंडोनेशिया की कैंडी फैक्टरी में भीषण आग: तीन की मौत; 36 कर्मचारी लापता, अपनों की तलाश में भटक रहे परिजन।

articles.title: एक किला, दो प्रतिद्वंद्वी शासक और इतिहास... दिल्ली के पुराना किले से पाकिस्तानी मंत्री ने क्या कहा
articles.summary: दिल्ली के पुराना किले में SCO सभ्यतागत संवाद मंच आयोजित हुआ। पाकिस्तान के जलवायु मंत्री डॉ. मुसादिक मलिक ने भाग लिया। उन्होंने हुमायूं और शेरशाह सूरी के उदाहरण से संवाद का संदेश दिया। दिल्ली के ऐतिहासिक पुराना किले में शनिवार को आयोजित शंघाई सहयोग संगठन (एससीओ) सभ्यतागत संवाद मंच में पाकिस्तान के जलवायु परिवर्तन मंत्री डॉ. मुसादिक मलिक ने इतिहास के जरिए भारत और पाकिस्तान सहित विभिन्न सभ्यताओं के बीच संवाद और आपसी समझ का संदेश दिया.
